LocalRpc service-endpoint mode (opt-in; parent-child unchanged, existing tests untouched): per-user well-known endpoint (Windows pipe with same-user protected DACL, network deny, PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS, first-instance protection; Linux UDS in a 0700 directory with SO_PEERCRED), peer identity resolved before HTTP/2 (pid-reuse and other-user refused), stream lane with back-pressure, per-method deadline profiles up to 120 s, 64 connections, idle rules. Real-OS tests on Windows and WSL2 incl. a 15-minute stream with 16 data calls; AOT 0 warnings. Hosted CI caught a BAN-POINTER finding and a ContentSandbox exhaustiveness guard (both fixed). Independent review (Opus 5.5): 3 rounds, APPROVE.

AR-02 evidence (development stage, not the full entry): the reviewer proved the Linux wrong-user refusal in WSL2 Debian without a second account (server uid 1000, client uid 1077 via setpriv as root): EACCES from the 0700 directory, and with the socket exposed the SO_PEERCRED uid check refused it (other-user=1). The Windows second-account token check stays open in AR-02; the runnable procedure (probe --ar02-serve/--ar02-connect) is in DesktopPlatform#187. Follow-ups for AF-NODE-01 (its scope: client library and auto-start): on Linux, connects beyond the backlog of 16 get EAGAIN, so ArcForges.Client must retry with bounded backoff and never treat EAGAIN as node-not-running (Design 02 §3 auto-start); test resolution of an elevated same-user client from a non-elevated node (fails closed as Unresolved today).
Security.Secrets Linux backends: Secret Service over session D-Bus, else a reported 0600-file fallback (desktopplatform-refactor section 2)

Merged DesktopPlatform#188 at reviewed head 5e17c4d (review of 6564ce22 plus the receipt's reviewer/decision text) as main 4e20932; cohort 1.0.0-ci.138.1 published. Security.Secrets Linux backends: Secret Service over the session D-Bus (Tmds.DBus.Protocol 0.94.1 admitted; DH session per the spec, plain only on NotSupported) and an owner-only file fallback (0700 run/secrets, 0600 files, atomic rename, symlink/ownership/permission refusal incl. the data root) with Protection=FileOwnerOnly; selection prefers Secret Service only when a default collection exists, records the reason. Real WSL2 tests with private dbus-daemon and gnome-keyring (opt-in) and the file fallback (CI); AOT probes on win-x64 and linux-x64. Windows backend unchanged. Independent review (Opus 5.5): 2 rounds, APPROVE.

Consumer obligations for the node (AF-NODE-02 sealing key and later account tasks), documented in the Secrets README: use SelectForCurrentPlatform (not CreateForCurrentPlatform) so the file fallback is chosen when Secret Service is unavailable; persist which backend holds each credential across runs (availability can change between starts); a locked keyring without a prompter fails closed (headless WSL with an existing login.keyring cannot store there); create the node data root 0700 (a group-writable root is refused, e.g. under umask 002). H-11 (gnome-keyring) is installed in WSL Debian, so the Secret Service leg ran.

Node store (docs/data/node-store.md): schema v1, expand-only migrations, min_reader, backups, command_dedup, sealed task secrets, env_snapshot, default policy; pins Contracts 1.0.0-ci.375.1+ and DesktopPlatform Security.Secrets 1.0.0-ci.138.1

Merged ArcForges#5 at reviewed head 0e2bcb2 as main 2217bb1; main CI and Security green. Node store: schema v1 (node-store.sql verbatim, 63 tables), forward-only expand-only migrations with min_reader refusal (store left byte-identical) and pre-migration backups, command_dedup with payload digests and FULL commits, AES-256-GCM sealed task secrets (task ID as AAD; node data key per version with its Security.Secrets backend), purge tombstones and STATE/secrets_unavailable (state.reason = purge instant), content-addressed env snapshots, default policy revision 1, expand-only CI step, store growth bench gate (43.29 MB per 10,000 attempts, hosted win-x64). Microsoft.Data.Sqlite AOT re-verified on win-x64 and linux-x64; ArcForges.Persistence.Sqlite stays Retain (no min_reader, store_ DDL denial, no WAL, no backups). Pins Contracts 1.0.0-ci.375.1 and DesktopPlatform 1.0.0-ci.138.1. Independent review (Opus 5.5): 2 rounds, APPROVE.

Follow-ups and design questions (not built): (1) NU1608 exception: DesktopPlatform Security.Secrets 1.0.0-ci.138.1 pins Contracts.Foundation exactly 1.0.0-ci.216.1 while the node needs 375.1; removal needs a DesktopPlatform cohort built on Foundation >= 375.1 (a DesktopPlatform change outside this range). (2) Design: growth-budget scope differs between 15 §2 and node-store.md §4 (hook_event rows and machine samples would add ~12 MB to the 43 MB measured; design-sized shells measured 45.3 MB). (3) Design: pre-migration backups keep purged task_secret values (purge vs backup retention, R-EXE-017 vs 13 §6). (4) Planning gap: default policy revision 1 leaves routing patterns, diagnosis actions and root/cache quotas empty; no task's scope adds them to DefaultPolicy, and revision 1 is written once per store, so later defaults do not reach existing stores — task proposal / Design question. (5) AF-NODE-01: payload digests hash wire bytes and map order matters, so client retries must resend identical bytes (or canonicalize); load the node data key at startup (secret-store I/O under the writer lock can block writes up to 25 s/2 min). (6) The expand-only check compares the branch with itself until a release exists; Linux store files are 0644 inside 0700 directories. (7) errors.md could note the key-unavailable use of STATE/secrets_unavailable (no details).

Known unresolved maintenance issue (Windows Credential Manager on the workstation, 2026-10-18). A stress reproduction on 2026-10-17 left Credential Manager entries created by that test. A read-only verification on 2026-10-18 found 746 listed entries whose names were all generated by the stress program, 13 other ArcForges.Secrets.v1 entries (preserved) and 14 unrelated credentials (773 in total). With the user's approval a bounded cleanup started: batches of at most 25, one delete at a time, each with a time limit and an absence check. It stopped after the first entry: the delete returned success in 1 ms and the absence check confirmed it, but that check took 1,248 ms (above the 1 s limit), and during the operation one other stress-generated entry appeared in the listing, so the listed counts were unchanged (746 stress entries, 13 preserved, 14 unrelated). The cause of the resurfacing is unknown. By the user's decision of 2026-10-18 (Option 1: stop) no further cleanup, deletion attempt, stress test or operation on orphan credential files is performed; the remaining entries hold random test values only; the 13 preserved ArcForges entries and all unrelated credentials are untouched. Design corrections of 2026-10-19 (ArcForges-Design #8, merge 78a5251), from the long-term evolution study requested on 2026-10-18. R-RES-012, Design 03 section 9, AD-0005 Windows 7 and 11 T-18 now limit escape detection to descendants whose recorded ancestry passes through a job member; launches through WMI, a broker, a service, a scheduled task or a spoofed parent are the documented gap T-23. Also new for this task: T-22 container tampering and the same-user qualifier on every resource guarantee (including the delivered Linux and Windows kill_tree capability reasons, which this task updates), T-26 privileged-change channels with the system bus in the channel catalogue, F-L04 trimmed to read-back and reporting, and F-W04. Scope, acceptance, verification, the Windows platform write path, future_validation and its matching risk were edited in this Plan change; position and dependencies are unchanged. Candidates for this task's own reviewer, not mandated by the study: explicit security descriptors on named jobs and ack events and refusal of an unexpected pre-existing root job (GUARDRAIL either way); EscapedProcesses.IsSameUser reading token facts (meaningful only with a confined tier); the F-L04 mechanism (explicit PrivateUsers=self on systemd 247-253, a fail-closed sentinel, `+`-prefixed record helpers, off under the Ubuntu AppArmor userns restriction). A real end-to-end test of the in-ancestry escaped path (T-18) is for this task's own design, since attempt jobs allow no breakaway.

The first half of the 2026-10-16 open design question (WMI-, broker- and parent-spoofed escapes invisible to the ancestry scan) is answered by ArcForges-Design #8 (78a5251, 2026-10-19): it is the documented gap T-23 (Design 11 section 1), and AF-SEC-01's acceptance and verification were corrected accordingly. The second half (an end-to-end test of the node-level escaped path for in-ancestry escapees, T-18) remains for AF-SEC-01's own design and review.
